oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Lifting Me Up or Holding Me Back: Black Women’s Experiences With Support or Lack Thereof in Social Work PhD Programs

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This study explores the unique challenges faced by Black women in research doctoral programs across the United States, particularly within social work programs. Despite their increasing presence in academia, Black women remain significantly underrepresented and often encounter systemic barriers that hinder their academic success and professional advancement. Utilizing critical race theory as a theoretical framework, this research highlights how these women experience intersectional discrimination and microaggressions, which shape their educational journeys. The study reveals that the definitions and manifestations of support among Black women in social work doctoral programs are deeply influenced by their lived experiences. Participants emphasized the importance of mentorship, community-building, and institutional advocacy as crucial elements of support that counteract isolation and promote resilience. By conducting a qualitative study, the authors are centering the voices and experiences of Black women (N=13) and contributing to a deeper understanding of the complexities of their academic experiences and underscores the need for transformative practices within higher education that foster equity and inclusion.
